content:
maya: Heads-up — saw a latency regression on the L4/A10 inference path for seqlen=512 after the kernel-autotune rollout last night. p50 jumped ~18% on a small set of canaries. Anyone else seeing this?

jon: I saw a small blip on our e2e smoke too, mainly when batch_size <= 2. p95 is fine, but p50 moved.

raj: Repro'd locally on an L4 VM. Notes: kernel_picker picked `fused_attn_v2_prechunk` for seqlen 512, batch 1. On A100/H100 the picker chose `fused_attn_v1` and latency was lower. KV cache hit rate also dropped ~10% in traces.

maya: Interesting — we usually favor v2 on memory-constrained devices. Could autotune be prioritizing kernel throughput over latency for small batches? :thinking_face:

elaine: Can you paste the profiler snippet, raj? Also which quant config?

raj: Pasting short trace: ```
Device: L4
Model: redwood-mini-7b
SeqLen: 512
Batch: 1
Kernel chosen: fused_attn_v2_prechunk
Avg step ms: 23.5 (baseline v1 on A100 = 19.8)
KV cache misses: 22%
Warp occupancy: 78%
SM stalls: mem_bound 14%
```

raj: On A10 the picker did the same as L4. On A100/H100 looked like v1 with higher occupancy and lower mem stalls.

jon: That suggests kernel selection heuristic is weighting flop efficiency rather than L2/mem behavior on smaller batches. Our batching heuristic maybe lowering preferred warp tiling.

maya: @elaine any recent changes to the kernel-scoring function? We pushed the autotune hyper for "latency_weight" from 0.6 -> 0.4 last week to favor throughput on mid-length sequences.

elaine: Yep, that was the change — intended to improve throughput on enterprise workloads. Didn't expect a p50 bump on small batch canaries. We can revert or make it device-scoped.

perf-bot: Regression detected: canary-suite/runtime-l4-smallbatch | latency p50 +17.9% | triggered at 2498765400 | cc: @eng-runtime 

maya: OK let's do a quick opt: add a device-aware override so L4/A10 keep latency_weight=0.6 for seqlen>=256 && batch<=2. We can roll as a soft flag first.

jon: I can push a preset override: ```json
{"preset_name":"smallbatch-l4-a10","selector":{"device_family":["l4","a10"],"seqlen":{"min":256},"batch":{"max":2}},"patch":{"autotune.latency_weight":0.6}}
```

elaine: +1. Also add a metric to autotune scoring that penalizes KV miss amplification — it's showing up when kernel prechunk changes memory access patterns.

raj: For the immediate canary, I ran a binary test: forcing kernel to v1 on L4 gave p50=20.1ms (better) but increases memory usage by ~8%. Tradeoff seems acceptable for small batches.

maya: Action items:
- jon: push preset override as canary (eng-runtime) — target: next 10% traffic
- elaine: add KV-miss penalty to scoring + run autotune sweep across L4/A10/A100/H100
- raj: run microbench (seqlen 256/512/1024, batch 1..4) and upload traces to the perf bucket

jon: Filed issue: https://internal.redwood/ops/ISSUE-6721 — will link PR.

elaine: If autotune scoring change is large, let's gate with runtime flag. We don't want to regress other workloads.

maya: Thanks all. If anyone hits a different kernel behavior (e.g., unexpected fallback to chunked kernels on H100), drop logs here. I'll monitor canary. :eyes:
